sections.history: Sholinghur is the Thirukkadigai of the Alvars and the ancient Ghatikachalam, one of the 108 Divya Desams in Thondai Nadu, sung by Peyalvar and Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Tradition holds that Narasimha gave darshan here to the child Prahlada and the Saptarishis for the span of one ghatika, about twenty-four minutes, and so devotees believe that worship offered for even a ghatika here is fruitful. The acharyas remembered at the shrine include Nathamuni, Ramanuja and Manavala Mamunigal, who is believed to have expounded the Thiruppavai here at the request of his disciple Erumbiappan.
sections.architecture: The temple crowns Periya Malai, the larger of two hills, rising some 230 metres above the plain; Yoga Narasimha is enshrined seated in yogic posture, the sanctum facing east, with Amirthavalli Thayar in her own shrine. A long flight of steps, well over a thousand, climbs the hill. The smaller hill, Chinna Malai, about 105 metres high, carries the shrine of Yoga Anjaneya, facing the great hill across the valley. At the foot of the hills lies the tank known as Thakkan Kulam.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the lord, in his Narasimha form, asked Anjaneya to help in slaying an asura, and then bade him remain on the smaller hill, seated in yogic posture, to grant boons to devotees — hence the second shrine. The name Ghatikachalam, the hill of the ghatika, recalls the brief span in which Narasimha gave darshan to Prahlada and the sages. A cherished tradition holds that in the month of Karthigai the lord, in yogic repose, opens his eyes.
sections.festivals: The month of Karthigai is the high season of the shrine, and its Sundays draw large numbers of pilgrims who climb the hill. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the Brahmotsavam are observed with processions, and the days of Peyalvar and Thirumangai Alvar are honoured. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The pilgrim's day begins at the foot of the hills with the long ascent, the whole valley opening out below. At the top, Yoga Narasimha receives the visitor in stillness. Many then cross to Chinna Malai for Yoga Anjaneya. Wear sturdy footwear for the steps, start early, carry water, and leave time for an unhurried, quiet darshan.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the foot of the steps. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Sholinghur is in Ranipet district, about 25 km from Arakkonam and reached by road from Arakkonam, Ranipet or Vellore (Katpadi); the hill temple lies just outside the town. The nearest major rail junctions are Arakkonam and Katpadi, and the nearest airport is Chennai.
